## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇika* ("Verses on offenses, training rules, and legal procedures", Pvr 19) is the nineteenth chapter of the *Parivāra* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It presents Vinaya material in the form of verse questions and answers, addressing specific offense categories and conditions—such as offenses tied to the rising of dawn, including *nissaggiya pācittiya* and *saṅghādisesa* [SuttaCentral; Bapat and Hirakawa 1970]. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
The text is expounded in the Vinaya commentary, the *Samantapāsādikā* (including its Chinese version, the *Shan-Chien-P'i-P'o-Sha*), which comments on its verses and analytical question-and-answer structure [Bapat and Hirakawa 1970]. In Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects considerable text reuse between the *Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇika* and the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vinayavinicchaya*, the *Vimativinodanī-ṭīkā*, and other sections of the *Parivāra* (such as the *Antarapeyyāla*, *Adhikaraṇabheda*, *Katthapaññattivāra*, *Ekuttarikanaya*, and *Katāpattivāra*), as well as the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments automatically with non-Pali materials, including the Sanskrit *Poṣadhavastu* and *Daśottarasūtra*, alongside Tibetan Vinaya works such as the *Vinayapraśnaṭīkā*, *Vinaya-uttaragrantha*, and *Vinayasaṃgraha* [DharmaNexus].
